query_ground_truth.workflow_task: Find a spreadsheet in OneDrive, download it, programmatically add comparison summary worksheets/sections, upload the modified workbook back to the same OneDrive item, and verify the cloud copy.
query_ground_truth.query: upload the updated workbook back to OneDrive and verify the cloud item
query_ground_truth.rationale: After modifying the spreadsheet locally, the agent needs to overwrite the existing cloud file and check its metadata to verify the update.

results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Required] [Prerequisite]: Decide destination folder reference (path/ID) and conflict_behavior (rename vs replace vs fail) before ONE_DRIVE_ONEDRIVE_UPLOAD_FILE (avoid unintended overwrite).

[Optional (if destination folder is unknown)] [Prerequisite]: Locate/confirm the target folder using ONE_DRIVE_ONEDRIVE_FIND_FOLDER (follow skip_token/next page); for keyword-only discovery use ONE_DRIVE_SEARCH_ITEMS (paginate as needed).
[Optional (if folders may not exist)] [Prerequisite]: Create missing folder segments using ONE_DRIVE_ONEDRIVE_CREATE_FOLDER (create parents before children).

[Required] [Prerequisite]: Ensure upload input is a staged object key for file.s3key (if starting from local/bytes, stage via COMPOSIO_REMOTE_WORKBENCH so ONE_DRIVE_ONEDRIVE_UPLOAD_FILE can fetch it).
[Required] [Step]: Upload using ONE_DRIVE_ONEDRIVE_UPLOAD_FILE (nested file{name,mimetype,s3key} + folder reference); capture returned item id/name/size for follow-ups.
[Optional (for verification)] [Next Step]: Confirm the upload using ONE_DRIVE_GET_ITEM (by returned id) or ONE_DRIVE_LIST_FOLDER_CHILDREN (presence/size; paginate until exhausted).

[Fallback (if overwrite must preserve item identity or direct upload fails)] [Fallback]: Use ONE_DRIVE_UPDATE_FILE_CONTENT to obtain an uploadUrl, then upload bytes via COMPOSIO_REMOTE_WORKBENCH (single PUT or chunked with Content-Range).
known_pitfalls: [ONE_DRIVE_ONEDRIVE_UPLOAD_FILE] Strict schema: file must be nested and include file.name, file.mimetype, and file.s3key or validation fails.
[ONE_DRIVE_ONEDRIVE_UPLOAD_FILE] file.s3key must reference an accessible staged object (not inline/base64 or a local/sandbox path); failures often surface as 404/403-style download errors.
[ONE_DRIVE_ONEDRIVE_FIND_FOLDER] Non-recursive and may paginate; ignoring skip_token/next page can falsely imply the folder doesn’t exist.
[ONE_DRIVE_SEARCH_ITEMS] Newly uploaded items may not appear immediately and results can paginate; use listing/get-by-id for deterministic verification.

[ONE_DRIVE_UPDATE_FILE_CONTENT] Creates/returns uploadUrl but does not upload bytes; upload sessions can hit HTTP 409 if one is already in progress, and uploadUrl can fail with 401 invalidSignature if stale.

reference_workbench_snippets.description: Upload a staged object using ONE_DRIVE_ONEDRIVE_UPLOAD_FILE (required nested file shape).
PUT bytes to uploadUrl from ONE_DRIVE_UPDATE_FILE_CONTENT (single-shot example).
reference_workbench_snippets.code:
```python
from urllib.parse import urlparse
import http.client, ssl
u=urlparse(upload_url)
path=u.path+('?' + u.query if u.query else '')
size=len(data)
c=http.client.HTTPSConnection(u.hostname,u.port or 443,timeout=60,context=ssl.create_default_context())
c.request('PUT',path,body=data,headers={'Content-Length':str(size),'Content-Range':f'bytes 0-{size-1}/{size}','Content-Type':'application/octet-stream'})
r=c.getresponse(); r.read(); c.close(); status=r.status
```

ONE_DRIVE_ONEDRIVE_UPLOAD_FILE.description: Uploads a file to a specified OneDrive folder, automatically creating the destination folder if it doesn't exist, renaming on conflict, and supporting large files via chunking.

name.description: The filename that will be used when uploading the file to the destination service

s3key.description: The S3 key of a publicly accessible file, typically returned from a previous download action that stored the file in S3. This key references an existing file that can be uploaded to another service.

mimetype.description: The MIME type of the file

file.description: The file to be uploaded, including its name and access to its binary content. Required if source_url is not provided.

folder.description: Destination folder path from root (e.g., '/Documents/Reports') or a unique folder ID. If the folder path doesn't exist, it will be created automatically (including any intermediate folders in the path).

site_id.description: The unique identifier of the SharePoint site to upload to. If provided, uses /sites/{siteId}/drive. Mutually exclusive with drive_id.

user_id.description: User ID (e.g., user_principal_name, unique GUID) or 'me' for the authenticated user, determining the target OneDrive.

drive_id.description: The unique identifier of the drive to upload to. If not provided, uses the default drive of the user_id. Mutually exclusive with site_id.

file_name.description: Name for the file in OneDrive when using source_url, including extension (e.g., 'report.pdf', 'image.png'). If not provided when using source_url, the filename will be extracted from the URL or Content-Disposition header. Ignored when using file parameter (filename comes from file.name).

source_url.description: Public HTTPS URL of the file to download and upload to OneDrive. Custom source headers are not supported. Required if file is not provided.

verify_ssl.description: Deprecated. SSL verification is always required for source_url downloads.

description.description: A user-visible description of the file. Only supported on OneDrive Personal.

defer_commit.description: If true, the final file creation is deferred until an explicit completion request is made. Useful for large files where you want to control when the upload is finalized.

if_match_etag.description: An ETag value to prevent lost updates. If provided, the upload will only proceed if the folder/parent's ETag matches this value. Returns 412 error if it doesn't match.

source_headers.description: Deprecated. Custom HTTP headers are not supported when downloading from source_url.

createdDateTime.description: The UTC date and time the file was created on a client. ISO 8601 format.

lastAccessedDateTime.description: The UTC date and time the file was last accessed. ISO 8601 format.

lastModifiedDateTime.description: The UTC date and time the file was last modified on a client. ISO 8601 format.

conflict_behavior.description: How to handle file name conflicts. 'rename' automatically renames the file if it exists (default), 'fail' returns an error, 'replace' overwrites the existing file. When renamed, the actual filename in the response may differ (e.g., suffixed with a number); use the response `id` or `webUrl` for follow-up operations.

ONE_DRIVE_ONEDRIVE_FIND_FOLDER.description: Finds folders by name within an accessible parent folder in OneDrive, or lists all its direct child folders if no name is specified. Search is non-recursive: only immediate children of `folder` are checked, not deeper hierarchy levels.

top.description: Maximum number of items to return in a single page. Use the returned next_page_token to fetch subsequent pages.

name.description: Exact name of the folder to find. If omitted, all direct child folders of the parent `folder` are returned.

expand.description: Comma-separated list of relationships to expand in the response (e.g., 'thumbnails', 'children'). See Microsoft Graph API documentation for supported expand properties.

folder.description: Path (e.g., '/My Files/Work', '/' for root) or unique ID of the parent folder where child folders are searched.

select.description: List of properties to include in the response (e.g., ['id', 'name', 'size']). Supports standard driveItem properties like id, name, webUrl, size, createdDateTime, lastModifiedDateTime, folder, etc. Note: 'folder' field is automatically included to enable folder identification, and 'name' is auto-included when filtering by folder name.

orderby.description: Sort results by specified properties (e.g., 'name', 'lastModifiedDateTime desc').

user_id.description: User's unique identifier (e.g., email, UPN) or 'me' for the authenticated user, specifying the OneDrive account.

page_token.description: Opaque continuation token for the next page. Omit for the first page; then pass back the `next_page_token` from the previous response, unmodified, until it is absent. Do not construct or edit it. When set, it drives pagination; resend the same required identifiers, but filter/sort params need not be repeated — the token carries them.

ONE_DRIVE_ONEDRIVE_CREATE_FOLDER.description: Creates a new folder in the user's OneDrive with configurable conflict behavior, optionally within a specified parent_folder (by ID or full path from root) which, if not the root, must exist and be accessible.

name.description: The desired name for the new folder (also accepts 'folder_name' as an alias). If a folder with this name already exists in the specified parent_folder, the new folder will be automatically renamed (e.g., 'New Folder' might become 'New Folder 1'). Examples: ['Annual Reports', 'Client Meeting Notes']

user_id.description: The user's ID, email, or 'me'. Defaults to 'me' (authenticated user). Required for S2S (app-only) auth.

description.description: Optional description for the folder. Provides a user-visible description of the folder. Examples: ['Project documents for Q1 2024', 'Meeting notes archive']

parent_folder.description: ID or full path of the parent folder for the new folder. Paths must start from the root (e.g., '/Documents/Reports'). If an ID is provided, it refers to an existing folder's unique ID. Examples: ['/Projects/Alpha', 'folder_id_12345ABC', '/']

conflict_behavior.description: How Microsoft Graph should handle a folder name conflict in the target parent folder. Use 'fail' to return an error, 'rename' to create a uniquely renamed folder, or 'replace' to replace the existing item when supported by Graph.
